title: Capability indexing — Retrieval-by-Procedure
description:
Retrieval-by-procedure searches for know-how rather than facts: given a goal phrased as an operation ('calibrate this sensor', 'migrate this schema'), it returns instructions, workflows, scripts, and programs known to complete it. The index is over capabilities — verbs, inputs, outputs, preconditions — not just keywords. Matching blends semantic understanding of the requested operation with hard checks that the procedure's requirements are satisfiable.

This record documents the capability indexing approach: Index procedures by (verb, input types, output types) triples so 'convert X to Y' queries match structurally.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
demo:
# Retrieval-by-Procedure demo: capability-triple matching with preconditions.
PROCS=[{"name":"migrate-sqlite-postgres","verbs":["migrate","convert"],"inputs":["sqlite"],"outputs":["postgres"],"pre":["disk>1GB"],"risk":"medium"},
       {"name":"backup-sqlite","verbs":["backup","copy"],"inputs":["sqlite"],"outputs":["backup"],"pre":[],"risk":"low"},
       {"name":"tune-postgres","verbs":["tune","optimize"],"inputs":["postgres"],"outputs":["postgres"],"pre":["dba"],"risk":"low"}]
CTX={"disk>1GB":True,"dba":False}
def find(verb,have,want):
    out=[]
    for p in PROCS:
        if verb in p["verbs"] and have in p["inputs"] and want in p["outputs"]:
            ok=all(CTX.get(c,False) for c in p["pre"])
            out.append((p["name"],ok,p["risk"],[c for c in p["pre"] if not CTX.get(c,False)]))
    return out
print(find("migrate","sqlite","postgres"))
print(find("tune","postgres","postgres"))
provenance: Public-harvest: documents established, real-world methods for retrieval-by-procedure; fact-checked public knowledge.

title: Outcome verification hooks — Retrieval-by-Procedure
description:
Retrieval-by-procedure searches for know-how rather than facts: given a goal phrased as an operation ('calibrate this sensor', 'migrate this schema'), it returns instructions, workflows, scripts, and programs known to complete it. The index is over capabilities — verbs, inputs, outputs, preconditions — not just keywords. Matching blends semantic understanding of the requested operation with hard checks that the procedure's requirements are satisfiable.

This record documents the outcome verification hooks approach: Pair each procedure with a check the caller can run to confirm the operation actually succeeded.

Teaching ladder rank 3 (advanced): this record covers production concerns — scaling behavior, failure modes, measurement, and the operational discipline needed to run this tool across a near-boundless archive.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
